title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: A tech-led selloff, hotter inflation readings, and a rising VIX leave markets vulnerable to sharp swings as midweek earnings, Treasury supply, and volatility settlement converge.
volatilityRationale: The VIX closed at 19.99 Friday after moving above 22 intraday, while the Nasdaq had its worst week since June, signaling a clear rise in hedging demand without a full panic regime. Wednesday's major-cap earnings, 20-year Treasury auction, and VIX-futures settlement are followed by Thursday claims and Friday's PMI, sentiment, and options catalysts, creating several opportunities for fast repricing.

recap.text: U.S. equities split sharply for the week: the S&P 500 fell 1.9% and Nasdaq 4.5%, while the Dow gained 0.7%; technology and AI-linked shares led the pullback.
The CBOE VIX closed at 19.99 on Friday after rising above 22 intraday, a marked pickup in expected near-term volatility as the tech selloff intensified.
September CPI rose 0.6% month over month and 3.7% year over year; core CPI increased 0.3% on the month, keeping inflation pressure in focus.
September PPI advanced 1.3% month over month and 6.3% year over year, reinforcing concern that price pressure may be broadening beyond consumer inflation.

The Federal Reserve released its October Beige Book on October 14, providing district-level business conditions ahead of the next policy meeting; it was an information release, not an FOMC rate decision.
Middle East supply and shipping risks kept energy prices in focus, adding a geopolitical channel to the week's inflation-sensitive market repricing.

triggers.text: September housing starts and building permits are due, offering a fresh read on rate-sensitive construction activity.
Meta, Tesla, IBM, Lam Research, and Texas Instruments report after the close; investors will scrutinize AI monetization, data-center spending, and guidance.
Treasury is scheduled to auction 20-year bonds, testing demand for long-duration government debt amid elevated inflation and issuance concerns.
October VIX futures reach their scheduled settlement, a volatility-market event that may matter more with spot volatility rising.
Weekly initial jobless claims will provide the next timely check on labor-market momentum.
October S&P Global flash manufacturing and services PMIs and final University of Michigan sentiment arrive, providing a growth and inflation-expectations check.

watch.text: Weekly SPXW options expire Friday; with flash PMIs and consumer sentiment on the same day, positioning and hedging flows could amplify the response to surprises.
No FOMC decision or minutes are scheduled this week; the next meeting is October 27–28, so inflation, housing, claims, and earnings will shape expectations into the meeting.
Monitor Middle East shipping and energy headlines: a renewed supply shock could lift inflation expectations and bond yields, while easing tensions could relieve that pressure.
